cards.explanation: The answer is False, friends, because the verse itself says it's a second time. The LORD appeared to Solomon, Israel's king, “…a second time, as He had appeared to him at Gibeon.” The first visit was at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:5). So this isn't the opening meeting. It's round two.

The answer is forever, friends. The LORD says He has consecrated the temple “…by putting My Name there forever…” Then He adds that His eyes and His heart will be there for all time. Forever and all time in the same breath. That's a promise with no end date on it.

The answer is his father David, friends. The LORD says to walk before Him “…as your father David walked…” David reigned over Israel before Solomon, and he was Solomon's father (1 Kings 2:11-12). The LORD describes that walk as one with a heart of integrity and uprightness.

The answer is throne, friends. God says that if Solomon walks as his father David walked, “…then I will establish your royal throne over Israel forever…” That's the seat of the king. And look at the word again: forever.

The answer is going off to serve other gods, friends. The LORD says that if Solomon or his sons turn away, “…and if you go off to serve and worship other gods…” then trouble follows. Turning away from God's commandments and going off to other gods are named together. It's the heart of the warning.

The answer is that He will cut Israel off from the land, friends. The LORD says, “…then I will cut off Israel from the land that I have given them…” It's a heavy line. It follows the warning about turning away.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “…and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name.” This comes after the warning to Solomon or his sons about turning away. So the temple itself is named in that warning.

The answer is as an object of scorn, friends. God says, “Then Israel will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.” That's a hard picture, and it's part of the warning. It comes after the part about turning away.

The answer is "Why has the LORD done this," friends. Those who pass by ask, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” I think this one hurts a little. It's a sad picture, and the next verse gives an answer.

The answer is Egypt, friends. Verse 9 says Israel forsook “…the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt…” It reminds them who He is and what He did. It's right there in the answer people give.
